search.placeholder: Search settings, e.g. root, port, theme
search.empty: No setting matches. Try another word.

theme.title: Theme
theme.desc: Saved to your account, so it follows you to any browser. Plugins can add more themes.

appearance.importFailedHint: Pick a JSON file exported from LinuxAdmin.
appearance.createHint: Starts from the current theme. Changes show live.
appearance.name: Name

colours.title: Colours
colours.desc: Per section gives every area its own colour. Distro colour uses the colour of your distribution everywhere. Themes marked “own colours” keep theirs.

follow.title: Follow the device
follow.desc: Switch between a dark and a light theme with your system setting.
follow.pair: Dark and light theme to use

density.title: Density
density.desc: Compact fits more rows in tables and lists.

motion.title: Reduce motion
motion.desc: Turns off widget wiggle, pulses and transitions.

refresh.title: Refresh live data
refresh.desc: How often live data such as the Overview charts and service lists updates. Faster uses more CPU.

terminal.colourDesc: Follow app uses the dark or light palette of the current theme.
terminal.snippetsDesc: The row of saved commands under the terminal.

notify.sshDesc: More than 10 in 5 minutes from the same address.
notify.browserDesc: Show them even when {name} is in a background tab.
notify.browserDenied: The browser blocked notifications. Allow them in the site settings.

server.askPassword: You'll be asked for your password the first time you change something.
server.unknownKeys: Unknown keys in the configuration file: {keys}.
server.warn: Changes here apply to every user of this server.

failed.title: Couldn't read the server configuration
failed.text: The daemon did not answer. Check that it is running and try again.

web.certDesc: Absolute path to a PEM certificate.
web.tlsDesc: Let's Encrypt needs a public domain name.

hosts.later: Managing other machines will arrive in a later version.
hosts.title: Machines you manage
hosts.addText: Another Linux machine reachable over SSH.
hosts.name: Name
hosts.userHint: Leave empty to use the same user name.

signin.rootDesc: Off is safer. Admins can still use sudo.
signin.showIp: Show IP address on the sign-in page
signin.showIpDesc: Anyone who opens the page sees it.
signin.unlockDesc: After this time without admin actions, sudo locks again.
signin.failuresDesc: Per address, for a few minutes.
signin.adminsOnlyDesc: Members of sudo, wheel or admin (and root, if allowed). Turn it off to let every local account in.
signin.allowUsersDesc: Also allowed, whatever their group. With no users, no groups and the switch above off, every local account may sign in. Changes also end the sessions of people who lose access, within a minute.
signin.allowUsersHint: Add a user name and press Enter
signin.allowGroupsDesc: Everyone in one of these groups, including their primary group.
signin.allowGroupsHint: Add a group name and press Enter
signin.badName: {name} is not a valid name (letters, digits, _ . @ -)

plugpol.unsignedDesc: Plugins not signed by the {name} team.
plugpol.devDesc: Load plugins from a folder and reload them on save.

about.versionDesc: A web console for Linux servers.

recent.title: Remember accounts on the sign-in page
recent.desc: Show the accounts used in this browser as tiles on the sign-in page. The names are stored in this browser only. Leave this off on shared computers; turning it off forgets them.

updates.title: Version and updates
updates.noRelease: No release has been published yet.
updates.noBuild: This release has no build for this machine ({arch}).
updates.packageBusy: Software is being installed or removed. The update can start when that has finished.
updates.adminOnly: An administrator can install it from here.
updates.managedUnknown: Updates are installed by the system package manager.
updates.managedDesc: {name} was installed as a distribution package, so it does not update itself. Install new versions the same way you installed it.

confirm.title: Update to {version}?
confirm.text: {name} will download version {version} ({size}), check its signature, install it and restart. This page reloads by itself when the new version answers.
confirm.signin: Everyone signed in to {name} on this server has to sign in again: sessions are kept in the server's memory and end with the restart.
confirm.interrupt: Open terminals, file transfers and other running tasks in the console are interrupted. The system itself keeps running.
confirm.rollback: If the new version does not answer within 30 seconds, the current version is restored automatically.

rollback.title: Previous version
rollback.desc: Version {version} is kept on this server so you can go back to it.
rollback.confirmText: {name} will switch from {current} to {version} and restart. This page reloads by itself when it answers.

state.rolled-back: Last update failed and was undone

run.title: Updating to {version}
run.rolledBack: Version {version} did not start, so the server went back to {from}. Nothing else changed. Reload the page and sign in again.
run.timeout: The server did not answer within 3 minutes. Reload the page in a moment; if it still does not answer, check `journalctl -u linuxadmin` on the server.

notice.title: {name} {version} is available
notice.detail: You are running {current}. Open Settings › About to update.

channel.title: Update channel
channel.desc: Pre-releases (release candidates, betas) arrive earlier and may have rough edges.

autoCheck.title: Check for updates automatically
autoCheck.desc: Administrators get a notification when a new version is out.

autoInstall.title: Install updates automatically
autoInstall.desc: {name} installs new versions by itself every day at this time, and restarts. Skipped while software is being installed.
autoInstall.managed: Not available: {manager} installs the updates of {name}.
